context: conveyor- & chute-driven circuit · dry (no-load) then wet (ore) commissioning

brief.intro: New to this project type? A mineral / mining processing plant (concentrator or beneficiation plant) takes run-of-mine (ROM) ore and reduces it through crushing, grinding and separation to produce a saleable concentrate. Unlike a normal industrial building, the plant is held together by its conveyors and chutes — every process stage only works if the material handling feeding it works first. The equipment itself (crushers, mills, flotation cells, thickeners) sits on massive foundations, and once erected it is proven twice: a dry, no-load mechanical run, then a wet run with real ore. Your schedule stands or falls on getting the crushing/grinding equipment and conveyor structure in early, and protecting the wet (ore) commissioning window, which is often tied to the mine's own production ramp-up.

scope.name: Enabling & site works
scope.desc: Earthworks, haul roads, laydown for abnormal-load deliveries.

scope.name: Civil & structural
scope.desc: Crusher/mill foundations, conveyor gantry & transfer-tower foundations, structural steel bins and hoppers.

scope.name: Crushing circuit
scope.desc: Primary, secondary and tertiary crushers with screens and feeders — reduces ROM rock in stages.

scope.name: Grinding (milling) circuit
scope.desc: SAG and ball mills with cyclone classification — grinds crushed ore to process-ready particle size.

scope.name: Material handling & conveying
scope.desc: Overland conveyors, stackers/reclaimers, transfer chutes — the connective tissue linking every stage.

scope.name: Separation & concentration
scope.desc: Flotation cells, gravity/magnetic separation, thickeners and leach circuit — recovers the valuable mineral.

scope.name: Slurry & process water
scope.desc: Slurry pumping, reagent dosing, process water and the tailings line.

scope.name: Electrical & instrumentation
scope.desc: MV substations, motor control centres (MCCs), variable-speed drives, SCADA/DCS.

scope.name: Testing & commissioning
scope.desc: Dry (no-load) mechanical commissioning, then wet (ore) commissioning to first concentrate.

must_get_right: It's conveyor- and chute-driven — get the material-handling route right first; every downstream process stage depends on its feeding conveyor.
Crushing/grinding circuit no-load (dry) proving must be complete before any ore is introduced — do not compress the dry-run gate.
Slurry and tailings systems (pumps, thickeners, tailings line) must be proven before wet commissioning — a failed slurry line stops the whole wet trial.
Protect the ore-commissioning window — first ore is often a one-shot event tied to the mine's own production ramp-up; re-trials cost real ore and real time.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Conveyor tie-in points and equipment-commissioning gates are carried as milestone activities so the network shows exactly which circuit feeds which.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and structural steel run a 6-day single-shift week; equipment erection may run extended shifts to protect the critical path; electrical and instrumentation works align to equipment readiness. Wet (ore) commissioning is scheduled around mine ore availability and typically runs continuous once started.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs equipment foundations → crushing/grinding equipment erection → conveying/material-handling tie-in → electrical & instrumentation → dry (no-load) commissioning → wet (ore) commissioning → first concentrate. Conveying is the connective tissue: no downstream circuit can be proven until the conveyor feeding it is running.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Mine/ROM ore availability is aligned to the wet-commissioning date; design is frozen and vendor equipment drawings are available before foundation design; the tailings storage facility is available ahead of wet commissioning.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Remote-site logistics and abnormal loads (mill shells, crusher frames) need route surveys and escorted transport; specialist mechanical-alignment crews for mills and crushers are a constrained resource; wet commissioning needs mine operations, process and maintenance teams together on site at the same time.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: long-lead equipment (mills / crushers) slippage, conveyor mis-tracking discovered late in dry commissioning, and ore availability slipping the wet-commissioning window. Schedule contingency is held before dry commissioning and before wet (ore) commissioning, not spread thinly across the network.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
